firmware.failed.what: report that bringing the mesh up failed, and cancel a play that was waiting on it rather than advancing a clock over a mesh that is not there

params.name: reason
params.what: what went wrong, said to the operator as it stands

firmware.failed.answers: Answers with nothing: it is a report, and what it changes is the status line and whether a waiting play is still waiting.

firmware.start.what: bring MeshCore up on every node that runs one, without starting the clock, so a mesh can be watched settling before any traffic
firmware.start.answers: The answer says the attempt began, not that anything is up: each node attaches on its own goroutine and the outcome arrives later as firmware.started or firmware.failed. Poll firmware.state to see how far it has got.

example.what: bring the mesh up before pressing play

firmware.started.what: carry the count of running firmware back into the world when an attach finishes, and tell whoever pressed play that pressing it again will now start the run
firmware.started.answers: `playing` appears only where a play was waiting on the mesh coming up, and is false: this reports that the mesh is up, and the next press of play is what starts the run.

firmware.state.what: ask how far along bringing the mesh up is, which is what every wait for firmware is built on
firmware.state.answers: `running` counts the processes that are up and `nodes` the nodes that run firmware at all, so a wait compares those two and never `total`, which counts every node in the scenario including the SDR observers and emitters that never boot one. `starting` is how many attaches are still in flight.

example.what: ask whether the mesh is up yet

node.provisioning.what: read the console lines a node is told before a run, so a region defined but never allowed to flood is visible rather than looking like broken radio

params.name: node
params.what: whose script to read; a name this network has not got is refused

node.provisioning.answers: `commands` is the lines that are actually sent, with the commentary dropped; the panel keeps the annotated form, each line with the reason it exists.

example.what: see what a node will be told at start

node.reflash_failed.what: report that a build change did not go through, which reaches the operator after the caller that asked has already been told it was accepted

params.name: reason
params.what: what went wrong, said to the operator as it stands

node.reflash_failed.answers: Answers with nothing: what it changes is the stats and the status line.

node.reflashed.what: report that a node's build change went through, refreshing the counters and the node's own window, which reads the node list rather than the stats and so showed the old build for ever

params.name: message
params.what: what to say, whose first word is the node that changed

node.reflashed.answers: Answers with nothing: what it changes is the stats, the node list and the status line.

node.set_firmware.what: change the build a node runs and apply it now, stopping the node, provisioning it and starting it again, because firmware is chosen when a node launches and nothing else would take effect

params.name: node
params.what: which node changes build; absent, blank or unknown is refused

params.name: version
params.what: the build to run, as the firmware library names it; absent or blank is refused

params.name: board
params.what: the hardware the image is for, because a board image is that image for that board; absent means a build for this machine

params.name: role
params.what: which MeshCore role the image is; absent leaves the node's role as it was

node.set_firmware.answers: The answer says the change was accepted, not that it took: the stop, provision and start run behind it, and a build that will not provision or a node that will not start arrives afterwards as node.reflash_failed.

example.what: put a host build on one node and restart it into it

node.set_firmware_only.what: record the build a node will run at its next start without touching the node now, for setting a fleet up before anything is launched

params.name: node
params.what: which node is set; absent, blank or unknown is refused

params.name: version
params.what: the build it will run, as the firmware library names it; absent or blank is refused

params.name: board
params.what: the hardware the image is for; absent means a build for this machine, and clears any board the node was pinned to

params.name: role
params.what: which MeshCore role the image is; absent leaves the node's role as it was

node.set_firmware_only.answers: Nothing restarts. A node already running goes on running what it has until something stops it, which is the difference between this and node.set_firmware.

example.what: choose what a node will run without disturbing it

node.start.what: bring a stopped node's firmware back up, which goes through the whole-mesh attach and so starts every other stopped node with it

params.name: node
params.what: which node starts; a name this network has not got is refused, and so is a node that is already running

node.start.answers: `started` is the node that was asked for, not everything that came up: the attach behind it skips only the nodes already running.

example.what: put a stopped node back on the air

node.stop.what: take one node's firmware down while leaving the node in the scenario, so it reports its final counters on the way out - which are usually the only evidence about a node that was misbehaving

params.name: node
params.what: which node stops; a name this network has not got is refused, and so is a node that is not running firmware

example.what: take one node off the air

nodes.stats.what: recompute every node's counters now rather than at the next tick, and answer with the rows themselves, which is how anything outside the window asks whether a node is running
nodes.stats.answers: `nodes` is how many rows there are and `stats` is the rows. A session with no engine built has no counters to report and answers with none, which is not a failure.

example.what: read every node's state and counters
